articles.headline: Major Skyrim Update Officially Comes to 'Elder Scrolls Online'
keyFacts: The Elder Scrolls Online has launched Season Two: Echoes of Skyrim, bringing new content and previously paid DLC into the base game.
The new season includes Western Skyrim exploration, the Greymoor Chapter, solo dungeon versions, and various rewards, running through January 27, 2027.
Additional content such as the Markarth DLC on November 9 and Update 52 on January 19 will arrive as the season progresses.
body: Skyrim is calling once again. The Elder Scrolls Online has officially launched Season Two: Echoes of Skyrim, bringing players back to the fan-favorite region with a fresh batch of content, including previously paid DLC that is now free for everyone who owns the base game.

Available now across Mac, PlayStation, Windows PC, and Xbox platforms, the new season of The Elder Scrolls Online runs through Jan. 27, 2027. Its launch brings the Greymoor Chapter and Wolfhunter DLC into the base game, opening up more of Tamriel without requiring players to purchase the expansions separately.
What's new in Season 2?

Greymoor is the headline addition for Skyrim fans, letting players explore Western Skyrim, visit the city of Solitude and venture into the subterranean realm of Blackreach. The Chapter also includes its storyline, the Antiquities system and the Kyne’s Aegis 12-player Trial. The Markarth DLC, which completes the Dark Heart of Skyrim storyline, will join the base game on November 9.

Season Two also introduces solo versions of two existing dungeons: Moon Hunter Keep and March of Sacrifices. Both feature Hircine-themed challenges, with difficulty options and new rewards for players who prefer to tackle dungeons without a group. The original four-player versions are also now accessible through the free Wolfhunter addition.

There are plenty of other rewards to chase, too. The new Tamriel Tome offers free and premium reward tracks featuring collectibles, currencies and items such as the Maarselok Slayer Mammoth mount. The Gold Coast Bazaar has also refreshed its selection of returning rewards, while seasonal events include the Witches Festival, Whitestrake’s Mayhem and the New Life Festival.

More content will arrive as the season progresses, including Skyrim- and Nowhere Vault-themed Golden Pursuits campaigns. Update 52, scheduled for January 19, will bring quality-of-life improvements such as increased furnishing limits for select homes, expanded Companion customization options and a new minimap interface option.

For players eager to revisit Skyrim while waiting for The Elder Scrolls 6, Echoes of Skyrim offers a convenient excuse to return to the province — or explore it for the first time — without paying extra for Greymoor or Wolfhunter. The new season is live now and runs through January.

articles.headline: Jalen Hurts' mom shares heartfelt message amid his blood clot diagnosis
keyFacts: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli.
His agent and team stated that he is clinically stable, expected to make a full recovery, and will likely miss the rest of the 2026 season.
His mother, Pamela Hurts, shared a video on TikTok asking the public for prayers and expressing gratitude.
body: Jalen Hurts' mom, Pamela Hurts, is speaking out amid the Philadelphia Eagles quarterback's blood clot diagnosis.
The NFL star's mom took to TikTok on Monday, Oct. 19, “Prayers work, prayers work. Keep praying," she said. "Keep praising God. Keep lifting his name up. Keep the faith, keep believing.”
“Just a reminder, y’all. Be grateful,” she said. “Be grateful for where you are and what you have because your life could change at a blink of an eye. Be grateful. What are you grateful for?”
Pamela captioned the video, “Things could always be worse…”
Jalen was diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and bilateral pulmonary emboli, which is when a blood clot travels to another part of the body, per the Cleveland Clinic.
Nicole Lynn, Jalen's agent, made a statement on Monday about his condition.

“After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is deep vein thrombosis as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli,” Lynn wrote. “He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations.”

Jalen was initially diagnosed with the blood clots during the Eagles' overseas game in London on Oct. 11 when they faced the Jacksonville Jaguars. He was cleared to play the game despite the team being aware of the blood clot. When the Eagles returned home, the clot had traveled from his leg to his lungs.
He will most likely miss the rest of the 2026 season.
What have the Eagles said about Jalen Hurts?
The Eagles also made a statement about Hurts' diagnosis and the future for the Super Bowl-winning quarterback.

“Jalen’s prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery,” the Eagles said on Monday. “We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when he is off blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects.”
The next Eagles game will be on Monday, Oct. 26, when they host the Dallas Cowboys.

articles.headline: It gives me great nerdly joy that the Next Fest demo on Steam's 100 most-played games list is a shopkeeping sim
keyFacts: The demo for the shopkeeping simulation game Probably Stolen reached Steam's 100 most-played games list with 34,230 concurrent players during Next Fest.
The singleplayer game involves running a grimy shop on a space station, scavenging for scrap, crafting items, and facing moral dilemmas.
PC Gamer reported that the full version of Probably Stolen is scheduled to launch next week on October 28.
body: As the sicko cartoon goes: "YES… HA HA HA… YES!" That's how I feel while peering at Steam's 100 most-played games list and spotting the Next Fest demo for shopkeeping sim Probably Stolen.

A singleplayer game about sitting behind a desk and managing inventory doing that well among the other 8,000+ demos that have arrived for Next Fest? So well it's actually charting with 34,230 concurrent players?
YES!

I played the demo back in September and loved it because it made me feel like I was running a corner store in Dredd or Cyberpunk 2077. You sit behind the counter of a grimy little shop on a space station and sell everything from food and beverages to weapons and cybernetic implants to a collection of interesting, unusual, and occasionally suspicious customers.

There's a bit of Fallout to it, as well: at night you can go and scavenge scrap and junk from trashpiles in hopes of adding something valuable to your inventory. You can do some crafting, too, smelting metals into ingots once you've got the gear for it, and this is the grim future so you can also start a rat farm and sell off the meat.

You can shop at other specialty vendors to acquire hard-to-find items to use or sell yourself, and there's even a bit of Papers, Please with the moral dilemmas you'll face: there's an underground movement fighting against the cyber-dystopia you can help or hinder, depending on if you want to turn a revolutionary in for a tidy bounty or keep your mouth shut if you spot someone on the cops' most-wanted list.

And don't worry, you don't need to be a huge sim geek to enjoy running the shop in Probably Stolen. The sim does go enjoyably deep, though: you can use a magnifying glass (Strange Horticulture style) to examine items for signs of counterfeiting, and even sell those counterfeit goods yourself to rich dummies who wouldn't know a legitimate cyber implant from a fake.
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

In other words, I'm pumped to see Probably Stolen getting so many players during Steam Next Fest, and you should become one of those players if you aren't already. There's not much longer to wait for the full game, either: Probably Stolen launches next week on October 28.

Chris started playing PC games in the 1980s, started writing about them in the early 2000s, and (finally) started getting paid to write about them in the late 2000s. Following a few years as a regular freelancer, PC Gamer hired him in 2014, probably so he'd stop emailing them asking for more work. Chris has a love-hate relationship with survival games and an unhealthy fascination with the inner lives of NPCs. He's also a fan of offbeat simulation games, mods, and ignoring storylines in RPGs so he can make up his own.

articles.headline: NFL exec believes Cowboys make sense as trade fit for ex-Eagles Super Bowl champion edge
keyFacts: An anonymous NFL executive told ESPN that the Dallas Cowboys would make sense as a trade destination for Arizona Cardinals edge rusher Josh Sweat.
The 2-4 Cowboys need edge-rush help to boost their defense and are considered contenders in the struggling NFC East division.
It remains uncertain if the Cardinals will trade Sweat, though the Cowboys could pursue a deal before the trade deadline if resources permit.
body: The Dallas Cowboys are 2-4 on the regular season, and yet, they're very much in the race for the NFC East title. While they've been struggling so far this season, there's reason to believe the Cowboys will be able to turn things around and win this division.
While the Philadelphia Eagles have so much going wrong right now, the New York Giants have a quarterback problem, and the Washington Commanders have one win, the Cowboys have room to grow.

This Cowboys season is far from over, and another trade could help. One NFL executive told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler that the Cowboys would "make a lot of sense" in a trade for ex-Eagles Super Bowl champion edge rusher Josh Sweat from the Arizona Cardinals.
Cowboys 'make a lot of sense' as a Josh Sweat landing spot
"As one team exec pointed out to me Tuesday, Josh Sweat makes a lot of sense," Fowler writes. "He fits Dallas' profile, and the Cowboys need edge-rush help."

With the Cardinals likely to be sellers, and Sweat's name popping up as a trade candidate over the offseason and leading up to the regular season, he'd make perfect sense as a trade target for Dallas.
They've invested a lot in the secondary and are waiting for some of their starters, like trade pickup Joey Porter Jr., to come back from injury.

If their secondary gets healthy, maybe all this team is missing is more pass rush help. Sweat, while maybe not the most prolific pass rusher and not of the same tier as Micah Parsons, could give Dallas a real boost up front.

While the Cowboys are in a bit of a predicament thanks to their trades over the years depleting their resources to make a trade, Jerry Jones has effectively gone all-in for the season, and seeing the team make another trade shouldn't be a surprise.

Will they actually make a trade for Sweat, or any other help on defense? It's possible. But the Cardinals haven't made it clear they're selling, and even if they do, Sweat might not be a part of the sell-off.
But if they do sell, and the Cowboys have reason to buy at this year's trade deadline, Sweat would make perfect sense as someone worth acquiring, just as this anonymous NFL executive speculated.

articles.headline: Fernandes rounds on Carrick after Man Utd humiliation
keyFacts: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes criticized head coach Michael Carrick's tactics following a 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como.
Fernandes told TNT Sports that the coaching staff chose not to press man-to-man and should have taken more risks.
Carrick responded in his press conference by stating that the team will not win if players do not run forward and back.
body: - Published
Manchester United skipper Bruno Fernandes turned on head coach Michael Carrick following one of the most humiliating nights in the club's European history.
A 4-1 Champions League hammering at Como led to Carrick fielding questions about his future.

He apologised to the 700 travelling fans, having ignored his beaten players after the final whistle to march across the pitch and repeatedly hold his hands up - in a manner similar to Ole Gunnar Solskjaer following a 4-1 defeat at Watford in November 2021 which led to his dismissal as United boss 24 hours later.

However, Fernandes - widely accepted as a football obsessive who watches games regularly as understands the tactical side as well as any player in the United squad - inflicted more damage when he spoke to TNT Sports.

"It's a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence," he told TNT Sports.

Asked directly whether Carrick got his tactics wrong, Fernandes added: "That's on the manager and staff to see, not me. Sometimes you have to be more brave under pressure, take the risk of pressing high and making them uncomfortable."

Told of Fernandes' comments in his post-match press conference, Carrick offered a curt response: "There's a little bit of whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you aren't going to win."
More to follow.

articles.headline: Iran says indirect talks with U.S. on ceasefire proposal continue
keyFacts: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said indirect negotiations with the U.S. continue over a seven-day ceasefire proposal.
The U.S. ordered non-emergency government personnel to leave Saudi Arabia due to escalating Houthi attacks, a spokesperson said.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he directed military and intelligence services to topple the Iranian regime.
body: What to know about the Iran war today:

- Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Wednesday that indirect negotiations with the U.S. continue over a seven-day ceasefire proposal that President last month, with the U.S. seeking new clauses.

- A senior official with Iran's Revolutionary Guard threatened Wednesday to target undersea internet cables in the Strait of Hormuz and other U.S. "investments" if the U.S. launches new strikes on Iranian infrastructure.

- Despite global oil prices remaining near five-month highs, President Trump insisted Tuesday that "we're doing very well" with Iran, adding that he was yet to "make a final decision of which way do we want to win" the war, "the nice way or the not nice way."
State Department orders some U.S. government employees and family members to leave Saudi Arabia
The U.S. has ordered all non-emergency government employees and their families to leave Saudi Arabia as the kingdom faces escalating attacks by Houthi militants.

"Iranian-supported Houthis have increasingly engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions," State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said in a social media post Wednesday.

The order came a few days after the , Bahrain, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates and several other countries warned that hostilities could rapidly and without warning spread beyond areas already affected by the fighting.
"The safety and security of Department personnel and their families remain our highest priority, and we will continue to take all necessary steps to protect and support them," Pigott added.
U.S. will suffer "even greater strategic failure" if it chooses war over diplomacy, Iranian FM says
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi issued a warning to the U.S. on Wednesday afternoon, saying it should choose diplomacy over returning to war.

"Iran is prepared to give diplomacy another chance if we see strong evidence of a sincere desire by US to build trust & reach a just solution," he wrote on X, sharing a link to an opinion piece in the Financial Times. "But if US chooses war over diplomacy, it'll certainly result in an even greater strategic failure."

Araghchi that Iran and the U.S. were still involved in indirect negotiations via mediators over the seven-day ceasefire proposal from September. The proposal was outright rejected by President Trump, but Araghchi said the U.S. was trying to add further clauses to the agreement.
U.S. sanctions Greek law firm for alleged involvement in Iranian "shadow fleet"
The U.S. Treasury announced new sanctions on the Panamanian-Greek law firm Karnakis and Karnakis for involvement in Iran's "shadow fleet" as part of its Operation Economic Outcast.

The U.S. accuses Karnakis and Karnakis of being indirectly involved in Iran's illicit shipping operations for years. A "shadow fleet" refers to oil tankers that hide their true ownership in order to evade sanctions.

"Whether you are conducting illegal oil transfers at sea or sitting in the corner office of a law firm, if you are supporting the Iranian regime, we will find you and sanction you," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a statement. "Iran's facilitators must make a choice: Either you are with us or against us. We know who you are, we know what you're doing, and we will continue to take action."

The Treasury also said it sanctioned Singapore- and UAE-based shipping agents, including a fleet of cargo vessels that has directly taken part in Iran's "shadow fleet" and "helped generate substantial revenue for the Iranian regime."
Riyadh airport partially reopens after deadly Houthi strike

A limited number of Saudi airlines took off and landed at the country's main airport on Wednesday, two days after authorities notified airlines that they could resume operations with prior permission.

Saudia and FlyNas were operating flights Wednesday, according to flight-tracking data published by FlightAware. Major carriers, including Lufthansa and Air France, have canceled flights through mid-November.
Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport has been hit multiple times this month by Yemen's Houthi rebels and shut down on Oct. 10. A strike two weeks ago killed 13 people and injured hundreds more.
The Houthis have acknowledged attacking the airport, claiming without evidence that Saudi Arabia provided military equipment to government forces through the facility.
Iran criticizes potential Egyptian involvement in Yemen war; Sisi promises only defensive actions
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said any interference in the Yemen war by Egypt or any other country would make the situation "more difficult."
"Egypt has sufficient experience to avoid entangling itself in such a highly complex conflict," said Iran's top diplomat in an interview with Iraqi state broadcaster Al-Iraqiya aired on Tuesday.
"We believe that any foreign presence or interference will only make resolving this issue more difficult," Araghchi noted.

Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said on Wednesday that Cairo's proposed military support for Riyadh was to "defend Saudi territory, and does not include an attack on Yemen," according to a statement from his office.

At a government event titled Egypt Forum 2026, Sisi said the "objective is to defend the kingdom's lands and borders, as well as those of any other Arab state, should it be requested of Egypt," his spokesman said in a statement.
Sisi on Saturday had asked parliament to authorize support for Saudi Arabia in its war with the Houthis, "if requested."
The parliament, which is stacked with supporters of the president, has since held two rare secret sessions, before postponing deliberations until next week.
Iran's new defense minister says first priority is meeting air force needs

Iran's newly appointed defense minister, Mehrdad Akhlaghi, said Wednesday his first hours in office were devoted to meeting the requirements of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps' Aerospace Force and the army's air defense units.

"We are not in a war of rhetoric in response to repeated threats; we are turning threats into greater readiness and more effective defensive power," he wrote in his first post on X since taking office.
Akhlaghi added Iran was concentrating on its objectives through the use of new technologies.
"We may eat dirt, but we will not give up our soil," he concluded.
Trump blocked Netanyahu's plan for multiday strikes on Iran, report says
President Trump blocked a planned Israeli multiday operation that would have resumed strikes against Iran on the weekend of Oct. 10, according to the Financial Times.

The plan was designed to exceed the intensity of the joint U.S.-Israeli military offensive launched in February, three people familiar with the matter told the paper, and would have struck Iranian nuclear sites, regime targets and civilian infrastructure such as power plants.
The president blocked the strike to avoid escalating conflict before the U.S. midterm elections, according to the report.
Iranian regime needs to be toppled, Netanyahu says
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Wednesday he had directed the Israeli army and intelligence services to topple the Iranian regime.
"The regime in Iran has still not learned the lesson," Netanyahu told a graduation ceremony at an officer training school in the country's southern Negev desert.

"Mojtaba Khamenei, the current tyrant, has decided to follow in his father's footsteps," he said, referring to the country's supreme leader, who replaced his father Ali Khamenei after he was killed in a U.S.-Israeli airstrike on Feb. 28.
"He has taken the safety off, and Iran is once again attempting to develop 'death bombs,'" he added, without giving details on what exactly he was referring to.

"There is only one way to remove this threat once and for all," Netanyahu said, "by toppling the regime in Iran. And that is my directive to the [Israel Defense Forces], the Mossad, and the security services."
He did not expand on how he expected the military or intelligence services to carry out the directive.
Saudi Arabia discusses deployment of up to 10,000 Syrian troops to Yemen

Saudi Arabia has held talks with a senior Syrian military delegation on arrangements to transfer up to 10,000 Syrian fighters to take part in the war against Yemen's Houthi movement, according to a report by the Lebanese Hezbollah-owned Al-Akhbar newspaper, citing Yemeni intelligence sources.

The report claims Syrian military officials visited Saudi Arabia's southern regions of Najran and Asir to inspect sites prepared to receive the fighters, while discussions in Riyadh covered transport logistics, financing and military assignments.

The Syrian delegation included Brig. Gen. Khaled Khattab, former commander of the Ansar al-Tawhid faction and current commander of the 82nd Division in the new Syrian army; and Brig. Gen.Haitham al-Ali, also known as Abu Muslim, commander of the army's Third Corps and a former leader in Hayat Tahrir al-Sham.

Khattab reportedly spent four days in southern Saudi Arabia, accompanied by Saudi officers, visiting sites in the regions of Asir and Najran being prepared to receive Syrian fighters. Meanwhile, al-Ali held several meetings with Saudi officers at the Defense Ministry in Riyadh to discuss the costs of transferring around 10,000 fighters, financial arrangements, additional benefits and their intended military tasks. The delegation reportedly finalized logistical arrangements for the transfer.
The report also raises the possibility that foreign fighters currently in Syria, including Uyghurs, Uzbeks, Tajiks and other nationalities, could be transferred to Yemen.
Iran taps missile industry figure as new defense chief, highlighting focus on weapons production
A missile industry veteran has been tapped as Iran's new defense minister, replacing the previous minister who was killed on Feb. 28, the first day of U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran.
Iranian parliamentarians overwhelmingly approved the appointment of Mehrdad Akhlaghi Ketabchi, 68, as the country's new defense chief on Sunday.

Akhlaghi studied chemical engineering at Amirkabir University of Technology and then spent more than four decades working in Iran's military industries, holding senior positions in the Shahid Bagheri Industrial Group, the Aerospace Industries Organization – which has worked on missile development in cooperation with Russia, China and North Korea – and the Defense Industries Organization.
He worked with Hassan Tehrani Moghaddam, a senior Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commander widely regarded as the father of Iran's missile industry.
Akhlaghi has been under international sanctions since 2007 because of his involvement in Iran's missile programs.

His appointment comes as Iran works to rebuild its military facilities and replenish weapons lost during the war. He has pledged to strengthen domestic arms production, and his background suggests rebuilding Iran's missile programs will be a priority for the ministry.

Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia has claimed repeatedly since late August that Iran has rebuilt its weapons manufacturing capacity, including last week, when it said the country was now able to make more arms than "even before it [the war] began."

Early in the war, the it had destroyed more than 85% of Iran's "defense industrial base," and President Trump had Iran's military capabilities were destroyed by U.S. strikes, but experts have questioned that assessment, and Iran has demonstrated an ongoing capacity to launch attacks on ships in the region.
Qatari aircraft leaves Tehran 30 minutes after arrival

A Qatari aircraft arrived in Tehran Tuesday just minutes after a plane carrying Pakistan's army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, departed. The Qatari plane left the Iranian capital approximately 30 minutes later, according to aviation tracking data cited by Iran's semi-official Fars News agency.

The aircraft's short stay raised questions about whether it might have been carrying a diplomatic message amid ongoing indirect negotiations between the U.S. and Iran. Qatar is among the nations that have acted as mediators between the two sides for months.
No information about the aircraft's passengers or why it was in Tehran for only half an hour was provided in the Fars report.
Houthis say they targeted Saudi operations room in Aden, southwest Yemen
Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels said they had targeted a Saudi military operations room at Badr Camp in Aden, in southwest Yemen, with a ballistic missile on Wednesday.
Houthi military spokesman Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree, in a post on X, called the strike a direct hit.
"Our armed forces successfully targeted the enemy Saudi operations room at Badr Camp in Aden with a ballistic missile. The strike was accurate and direct," he said.
Aden is the de facto seat of power of Yemen's Saudi-backed government, which was forced to decamp after the Houthis occupied the national capital Sanaa more than a decade ago.
The attack claimed by the Houthis Wednesday was the third in a week on Aden.

A police official in Aden told the French news agency AFP earlier that there had been a blast "caused by a Houthi missile." Two other security sources told AFP the strike targeted a site near the city's airport.
Iran threatens undersea internet cables in Strait of Hormuz
A senior official from Iran's Revolutionary Guard threatened to target undersea internet cables in the Strait of Hormuz if Iranian infrastructure comes under attack.

Brig. Gen. Yadollah Javani, the IRGC's deputy for political affairs, warned Iran would use its full capabilities to retaliate if the U.S. and its allies launch new attacks against Iranian infrastructure. He said various investments and assets, including undersea cables carrying internet data in the strategic waterway, could be among the targets of Iranian retaliation if hostilities resume.

"The Americans and their allies have significant investments, and if they want to damage our infrastructure, it is natural that the Islamic Republic will use all its capabilities and easily destroy their investments and assets, including the internet cables that pass beneath the waters of the Strait of Hormuz," he said.
Analysts say cutting the cables in the waterway would most likely affect internet connectivity in Persian Gulf countries.
Iran says Tehran and Washington still engaged in negotiations, ceasefire proposal still in play

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Wednesday that Tehran and Washington were still engaged in indirect negotiations via mediators over the seven-day ceasefire proposal presented by Iran in September.
Araghchi said the U.S. was seeking to add further clauses to the Iranian proposal, which Mr. Trump rejected last month.

The proposal called for the end of the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports and vessels, the lifting of sanctions on Iranian oil sales, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and the release of frozen Iranian assets.
He said Pakistan and Qatar were among the nations facilitating the indirect talks between Iran and the U.S., as they have been for months.
"The negotiating table remains in place," Araghchi said. "It is the American side that is closing the path, not Iran."
U.S. ramps up warnings to Americans in Middle East after deadly Houthi strikes

U.S. diplomatic missions across the Middle East have issued a new round of security warnings to Americans amid escalating attacks by Iran-backed Houthi militants against Saudi Arabia, including an Oct. 10 strike on Riyadh's international airport that killed an American citizen.

The alerts, issued Sunday by U.S. embassies in Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates and several other countries, warned that hostilities could rapidly and without warning spread beyond areas already affected by the fighting. The advisories urged Americans to exercise vigilance and prepare for possible flight cancellations, airspace closures and other travel disruptions.

"We are actively warning U.S. citizens about the very real threat the Houthis pose and urging them to heed official guidance," Edgar Vasquez, the State Department's deputy assistant secretary for press, told CBS News.

"These alerts are part of a proactive effort by the Trump administration to ensure Americans are aware of potential risks," Vasquez said, adding that the safety and security of American citizens remain the department's "top priority."
Trump says he's deciding how to win Iran war: "We're doing very well with Iran"
President Trump said the U.S. is "doing very well with Iran" and he's just deciding how he wants to win the war.

"As you know, we're doing very well with Iran," Mr. Trump said as he took questions from reporters in the Oval Office at an unrelated executive order signing. "We just have to make a final decision of which way do we want to win? Do we want to win the nice way or the not nice way? But we're doing very well."

The war, which Mr. Trump said would take only a few weeks in March, has now dragged on for almost eight months with no apparent end in sight. Iran said on Tuesday it unless the U.S. drops its sanctions, threats and pressure campaign — an unlikely demand.
The president also discussed Europe not helping the U.S. with the war with Iran, saying, "We don't need any help. But I was testing them."

"I just called individual presidents and prime ministers to ask, would they like to help us? And they said, 'No,'" Mr. Trump said. "I said, 'Well, that's not nice.' You know, we spend hundreds of billions a year on NATO. And they said no."

articles.headline: Bayern Munich v Arsenal: Champions League – live
keyFacts: Eberechi Eze scored the opening goal for Arsenal after a VAR review confirmed he was onside following a pass from Martin Odegaard.
Alphonso Davies equalized for Bayern Munich by scoring past goalkeeper David Raya after receiving a long pass from Harry Kane.
Both goalkeepers and defenders made crucial saves and goal-line clearances during a fast-paced first half of the Champions League match.
body: 52 min: Tah plays a long pass down the left to find Saibari, who enters the Arsenal box before scuffing his shot. Saibari’s got himself into some good positions tonight, only to … well, that’s a start, though, isn’t it?

50 min: … and now it’s Raya’s turn to make an outstanding stop! Gnabry crosses from the right. Upamecano powers a header goalwards; from point-blank range, Raya somehow parry-scoops away! Two of the finest saves you’ll see in a long while!

48 min: … but Arsenal have come back out with intent, too, and Eze wins the first corner since the restart with a dribble down the left. Rice hits it long. Guimaraes wins a header at the far stick, six yards out. He plants a downward header towards the bottom right. It’s surely a goal, but Neuer somehow shovels it up off the line, off the crossbar, and away. What a save! Not quite on the Banks-Pele level, but not far off!
46 min: Kane is quickly on the ball, nearly releasing Gnabry down the middle with a route-one pass. Gabriel is on point to intercept. So close to a super-fast start to the second half for the hosts.
It took a while for his match to get going, but it was worth the wait. Odegaard to Eze was sensational; so was Kane to Davies. Good luck predicting the outcome of this.

45 min: Kane plays a cute pass round the corner to release Gnabry down the right. Davies is free on the left, but Gnabry opts to shoot from distance. Poor decision. His effort is deflected out for a corner, but Davies had Raya and the goal in his sights. There will be two additional minutes.

44 min: Davies is everywhere at the moment. He barrels down the left and earns Bayern a corner. Gnabry whips towards the near post, where Timber heads clear. Bayern have been much improved in the last few minutes; what a difference a goal makes.

42 min: Rice’s delivery skims off the top of Laimer’s head at the near post. The ball nearly loops into the bottom right. Calafiori tries to force it home, but can only ripple the side netting. Laimer gets away with a big one there, because for a couple of split seconds, that had own goal written all over it.

39 min: Kane is caught late by Konsa’s lunge on the halfway line. Bayern are gifted the advantage, but Davies and Gnabry aren’t able to combine as they barrel towards the Arsenal box. Rice gets in the road to nix the attack. Then Konsa goes into the book. Kane is not happy with his England team-mate.

37 min: That was a peach of a goal. What a finish! But what a pass! Good luck deciding which of the Odegaard-Eze and Kane-Davies combinations is the most outrageously good. You could spend all night debating it. The assists and finishes so far tonight have been from the top drawer.

… so having said that, they split Arsenal open with absurd ease! Another Kane pass from deep. Almost from the centre spot, he forensically rolls a pass down the inside-left channel to release Davies, who gets in ahead of last man Timber, opens his body upon reaching the edge of the box, and passes across Raya and into the bottom right!
32 min: Bayern are struggling to play out from the back. Arsenal’s press too much for them. A couple of long hoicks forward that come to nothing. Mikel Arteta will be delighted right now.

30 min: … and sends it long. This time it’s Guimaraes level with the far post, six yards out. He shins his volley wide left. He joins Calafiori in the Should Have Scored column, and from exactly the same blade of grass as well. Bayern haven’t dealt with these corners at all.
29 min: Bayern haven’t responded to that blow. They’ve not managed to get forward at all. And now Madueke probes down the right to win another Arsenal corner. Odegaard comes across to take …

27 min: The goal was initially ruled out for offside, but VAR double-checked and turns out Stanišić was playing Eze on. The substitute hasn’t taken long to make his presence felt. And what a pass forward by Odegaard!

Odegaard mid-irons a long fade down the left to release Eze. As simple as that! Eze enters the box, takes his time, lets the ball sit up twice, and larrups a low bouncer across Neuer and into the bottom right!

23 min: Kane quarterbacks another fine long pass from deep, finding Saibari inside the Arsenal box down the inside-right channel. Saibari can’t control. Goal kick. Bayern must wish Kane could somehow launch these passes to himself.

21 min: Bayern launch a quick counter, Kane taking the goal kick, spraying a pass down the left for Davies. The ball’s shuttled to Gnabry down the inside-right channel. Gnabry enters the box and shoots low and hard towards the bottom left. Raya saves well, but that should have been a goal as well. Somewhere in the multiverse, it’s 1-1 after a short-order exchange of goals.

20 min: Odegaard swings in from the right. Neuer comes for the ball and flaps. The ball drops to Calafiori, six yards out, level with the far stick. Calafiori should score, but leans back and hoicks over. What a miss!

17 min: Davies dribbles hard down the left and enters the Arsenal box. Gabriel sticks to his shoulder, so Davies can’t get a shot away from a tight angle. Gabriel flicks the ball out for a corner … but Bayern strangely don’t get it.

15 min: Kim pings a speculative pass down the left for Davies, who nearly manages to nip past Timber at high speed, only for the defender to give him a gentle tap on the back, one that causes him to take an extra step that sends both ball and player over the byline. Goal kick. Saucy defending.

12 min: “Word precludes me from tuning in on Paramount+ in the States,” begins Jeff Necessary, Gunner in North Carolina, “so keeping the MBM open for occasional checks. Given the way Arsenal first halves have gone lately, I may not miss much for a while.” Well, Jeff, you’ve got that damn straight at the moment.

8 min: Saka spins Davies down the right, but the Canadian international comes back at his man to ensure the Arsenal winger doesn’t enter the box. Saka nips infield instead, then takes a clumsy prod at the ball before grabbing his thigh and crumpling to the floor in pain. This doesn’t look great.

6 min: Saka and Havertz combine down the inside-right channel, the latter entering the Bayern box. Havertz scuffs a cross; Saka can’t force the ball home from the middle of a melee on the edge of the six-yard box. Bayern clear, but Arsenal will be very happy with these early attacks.

4 min: Raya passes long. Timber cushions a header in from the right for Saka, who shuttles the ball further across towards Madueke. For a second, it looks like Bayern have been opened up with a couple of simple passes, but Madueke clanks into Laimer and the danger is gone.

Vincent Kompany and Mikel Arteta worked with each other at Manchester City. When the former emerges from the tunnel, the pair embrace warmly and have a quick catch-up. And then Arsenal get the game started.

The teams are out! Bayern are in one of their all-red phases, while Arsenal are harking back to the early 90s with a blue version of the famous bruised banana. Vincent Kompany is in the house, by the way, having recovered from a virus that threatened to keep him in bed. And so is Germany boss Jurgen Klopp, in the stands flashing that smile and throwing his arm around the shoulder of another erstwhile Liverpool manager, Rafael Benitez. Everyone having a good time, it seems, and looking forward to this big showdown, including Arsenal fan Charles Antaki … well, kind of: “Pretty dismal, the fare served up in the game against Forest. But! Pundits have assured us that because Bayern are going to be on the attack, Arsenal will be free to entertain us with a dazzling display of skill, ambition, irresistible cheeks and above all, goals. Not much to say about that except We Shall See.” We’ll be off in a minute or two.

Mikel Arteta speaks to TNT Sports. “We’re gonna have to play, I expect, three or four different games at different stages … we need everybody ready because we need to change and adapt to that … freshness … very excited … we have talked about our enthusiasm for playing on these big stages … that’s where you want to get tested … play with a lot of courage … a lot of aggression … be decisive … we have prepared for what we have to do.”
There are plenty of other Champions League matches about to kick off tonight. Sarah Rendell has you covered in the latest edition of your super soaraway Clocko. Get on it!
Look at that bench; Arsenal’s squad goes deep. Which doesn’t necessarily explain the headline below … but it can’t not help. The good people o’ Opta explain all.

Bayern are without Joshua Kimmich following a death in his immediate family. Harry Kane leads the line, while former Liverpool winger Luis Diaz is on the bench. Michael Olise is suspended following his two-yellows-in-two-minutes fiasco during the 3-3 draw at Viking.
Arsenal make two changes to their starting XI following the staunch 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest. Noni Madueke and Jurriën Timber replace Eberechi Eze and Ben White, who drop to the bench.

Arsenal’s last three visits to Munich have ended badly. In reverse order: 0-1 (2024), 1-5 (2017), 1-5 (2015). All three worthy of a large bräukeller-infused GULP. On the other hand, Arsenal won the last meeting between these two sides, 3-1 last November at the Emirates, and they go into this match having won 10 of their 11 games in all competitions so far this season. Bayern by contrast aren’t at their usual steamrolling best: OK, they’ve just mullered RB Leipzig 6-1, but before that they dropped Bundesliga points at Augsburg (2-2) and should really have been beaten by Viking in a 3-3 draw last week. So both teams have positives to draw on and negatives to try their best to ignore. Kick-off is at 8pm BST. It’s on!

articles.headline: Meta fined $25bn for 'lies' over user data privacy
keyFacts: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay a $25 billion fine for misleading the public about its user data privacy practices.
A jury found Meta violated state laws over 40 million times by sharing user data without permission over 11 years.
Meta's head lawyer stated that the company intends to appeal the ruling, claiming the appeal will be successful.
body: - Published
Meta, the company behind Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp has been hit with the largest ever fine against it for its business practices.

A judge in New Mexico on Wednesday ordered the company to pay $25bn (Â£18.6bn) following a two-week trial earlier this year that found it had spent years lying to the public about how it handled Facebook user data.
"The lies extend beyond Facebook's data practices as well," the judge said, adding they went to "the heart of Facebook's core business practices".
Meta's head lawyer CJ Mahoney said the ruling made it "all but impossible to do business in the state of New Mexico". The company intends to appeal, a move Mahoney said will be successful.
The fine is the largest to date against Meta, which has either been fined or agreed to settle several other lawsuits this year, including an $18bn deal with California over child safety.
New Mexico's lawsuit stemmed from the role of Meta, then still doing business as Facebook, in what became known as the Cambridge Analytica scandal.

That firm utilized data and information from millions of Facebook users as part of its work in political consulting, including on work related to the 2016 US Presidential election, which saw Donald Trump elected for the first time.

New Mexico had also accused Meta of intentionally misleading the public on how it benefitted from content that included hate speech, and how such rules against it were enforced. The jury found the company had intentionally misled the public on those claims, too.
Meta disputed those accusations. "At its core, this lawsuit seeks to impose a tax on speech to enforce new rules for what people can say online," Mahoney added.

Lawyers for New Mexico sued the company over many statements Meta executives had made over the years that user data was never shared with or accessed by third parties without a user's permission, when in reality it had been.

They claimed that the entire population of the state, roughly two million people, was impacted by Meta's dishonesty regarding the way it controlled user data. A jury found that Meta had violated state laws more than 40 million times.
"For too long, powerful technology companies have operated as though their size and influence put them beyond the reach of the law," New Mexico Attorney General RaÃºl Torrez said Wednesday.
"Today's result makes clear that no corporation is too powerful to be held accountable."
The state lawyers sought up to $40bn in fines against Meta. Meta had argued anything beyond $3.4bn would be unconstitutional.
Judge Francis Mathew on Wednesday was direct in his decision to fine Meta an amount roughly equal to its profits each quarter.
He said Meta's violations of law and misrepresentations to the public about how their Facebook data was used and shared were "willful" and spanned "more than 11 years", stretching from 2010 to 2021.
Communications between senior executives, including Mark Zuckerberg, were "designed to mislead the public", Judge Mathew wrote in his order.
While the full amount of the penalty against Meta, based on thousands of violations of state law, was calculated as $219bn, Judge Mathew reduced the penalty to the $25bn fine.
It follows a $5bn fine levied by the US Federal Trade Commission in 2019 against the company over its data privacy practices.

New Mexico has been one of Meta's most notable adversaries in court. The state this year also fined Meta almost $1bn for misleading the public about the safety of its social media platforms for children.
The judge overseeing that lawsuit ultimately compared Meta to an industrial polluter of the air, with its form of pollution being "the psychological harm and sexual exploitation of children".
California and several other states had collectively sued Meta over similar issues related to a lack of child safety features on Meta's platforms and resulting harms to children.
Meta and the states reached a mutual settlement deal, which did not include a fine or any admission of wrongdoing, to end that case only a few days into what was expected to be a multi-week trial.

articles.headline: Airbnb bans making guests do dishes and take out the trash
keyFacts: Airbnb updated its house rules policy to ban hosts from requiring guests to complete time-consuming checkout chores starting with reservations booked on or after November 20th.
Hosts are now limited to reasonable requests such as placing used dishes in the sink, gathering towels, sorting indoor trash, and turning off utilities when leaving.
Airbnb is displaying rules more prominently on listings with a new section, and some hosts have pushed back against the restrictions on company forums.
body: Checking out of your next Airbnb might be less of a hassle now that the company is banning hosts from including time-consuming chores in their house rules. Airbnb’s updated house rules policy, which starts with reservations booked on or after November 20th, says hosts can’t ask guests to “complete tasks that require significant effort or time, or would typically be performed by a cleaner.” According to Airbnb, that includes:
Airbnb bans making guests do dishes and take out the trash
Airbnb’s new rules limit hosts to ‘reasonable’ requests like putting dirty dishes in the sink.
- Dishes: Guests shouldn’t be asked to wash and put away dishes, but you can ask them to put used dishes in the sink.
- Laundry: Guests shouldn’t be asked to remove sheets from the bed or start a load of laundry, but you can ask them to gather used towels.
- Trash: Guests shouldn’t be asked to take garbage off-site, but you can ask them to separate their trash and recycling into designated indoor bins.
- Utilities: Guests shouldn’t be asked to avoid using a listed amenity like air conditioning, but you can ask them to turn it off when they leave.

Airbnb is displaying hosts’ requests more prominently now in a new “rules and requests” section on listings. You might see an “includes cleaning requests” warning if a host leaves chore requests in their listing after the new policy goes into effect. Hosts aren’t allowed to sneak in extra rules in messages to guests or on signs around their property, either.

Some hosts pushed back on the house rules restrictions on Airbnb’s forums, saying they pose health risks and arguing that guests can simply choose not to stay at listings with overly-strict rules. Airbnb says there can be exceptions to the limits on checkout chores, like asking guests to “dispose of trash in an animal-proof container in bear country.”

body: Xbox is previewing paid cloud gaming for players without Game Pass

Xbox has been overhauling several of its gaming offerings in recent months as the company pivots under its new leadership. One of the upcoming changes is to cloud gaming, with plans to apply time limits of five to 15 hours for how long Game Pass subscribers can stream each month. In advance of those changes in November, Xbox is rolling out early previews of cloud playtime for people in its Xbox Insider program who don't have a Game Pass subscription. Xbox Insider lets players try out features early and provide feedback ahead of their official launch.

During this phase, players can purchase cloud gaming access in blocks of 10 hours for $4, 25 hours for $8 or 50 hours for $12. Those rates are being called the "introductory launch prices," so it's possible the final costs could still change next month when Game Pass subscribers will also have to pay to go beyond the new time limits.

Cloud playtime purchases unlock "an ad-free cloud gaming experience, including shorter wait times, high-quality streaming, and playtime that remains available until it's used." People in the Insiders program have also been able to try ad-supported cloud streaming for free since the summer.

articles.headline: GM is betting compute and AI will help it compete with Chinese automakers
keyFacts: General Motors announced a new fourth-generation EV platform centered on advanced software, AI, and a powerful central computing architecture.
Sterling Anderson said the technology aims to make vehicles helpful everyday spaces that understand context and reduce friction.
The technological overhaul and a hands-and-eyes-free autonomous highway driving feature are scheduled to debut in 2028 with the Cadillac Escalade IQ.
body: When GM announced its new fourth-generation EV platform on Wednesday, what the automaker didn’t share was almost as notable as what it did.

The new EV platform, part of a series of technology-focused announced during its annual GM Forward event in New York, didn’t talk about suspension geometries, dash-to-axle ratios, and torsional rigidity, all nerdy automotive terms that translate to how people will experience a car. Is it supple or sporty? Does it have a refined stance? When it hits a pothole, does it feel like a bank vault or a paper plate?

Instead, GM’s announcement centered on novel battery chemistries, revamped electric motors, and an entirely new central computing platform and electrical architecture that will connect every system in the car, including acceleration and power, steering, braking, and active safety features as well as software. Lots and lots of software.

“We think vehicles can become a more capable and helpful part of everyday life if we make them spaces that understand context, reduce friction, and give people back moments that would otherwise be consumed by the demands of the road,” Sterling Anderson, executive vice president, global product, and chief product officer at GM, told TechCrunch in a recent interview.

That sure doesn’t sound like a traditional automaker’s pitch. Then again, since the arrival of Tesla, Rivian, and Chinese automakers, the industry hasn’t been the same. Ride and handling still matter, but they’re table stakes. What sets vehicles apart today is largely defined by software.

Anderson has talked about this future GM before. Last year, the company announced plans to overhaul the electrical and computational guts of its future vehicles in a bid to deliver faster software, more capable automated driving features, and a custom, conversational AI assistant.

This year, GM is providing more details and dates. This technological overhaul is set to debut in 2028 with the Cadillac Escalade IQ. The company will also rollout an autonomous highway driving feature in 2028 that will allow drivers to have their hands and eyes off the road and without the need to be ready to take over.
The software race includes hardware

European and U.S. automakers have spent years chasing the prospect of software-defined vehicles, but have often fallen short. Volkswagen Group had so much trouble with its own in-house effort, including its troubled Cariad unit, that it struck a $5.8 billion joint venture deal with relative newcomer Rivian.

GM has been on its own capitally intensive software adventure. The company has bet heavily on software in recent years. It ditched the popular smartphone projection technology Apple CarPlay for nearly all of its EVs, and instead turned to a Google-based infotainment system, which is actually quite capable even if it doesn’t yet live up to the standards set by Tesla and Rivian.

It’s poured billions into software and autonomous vehicle technology development too. GM’s capitalized software amortization expense in 2025 was $866 million, which gives a sense of how much it is spending even as it spreads out the cost over years.
Like many legacy automakers, GM has come to the conclusion that the old approach to electronics, which scattered computer chips throughout the vehicle, was holding it back.

For fourth-generation EVs, GM will centralize much of those functions on a Central Compute Unit (CCU) that’s 40-times more powerful than its existing systems. Eliminating smaller chips on the edges will help trim wiring by 30%, saving weight and simplifying assembly.
GM notes that this new CCU will work on fossil fuel models, too, though it will debut in the Cadillac Escalade IQ, a vehicle that is shaping up to be the automaker’s technological flagship.

The CCU will handle the usual propulsion and chassis controls, but also perception and active safety. That should help pave the way for more advanced autonomy features, which GM also announced on Wednesday.
Such a move was perhaps inevitable. Pressure on automakers has been building on all sides.
Domestically, Tesla has been pushing the boundaries of autonomy, in part because it developed a true software-defined vehicle.
Automakers like GM are also feeling pressure from Chinese manufacturers, which have shortened development cycles to two to three years, down from the usual four to five years.

GM intends to match that cadence. Alongside announcements about battery chemistries and autonomy, GM outlined how enterprise AI tools have sped up vehicle development across every sector as it pushes to slash its traditional four-to-five-year development timeline in half.

GM gave a brief glimpse of its revamped development strategy. One example: engineers went through 300,000 virtual designs of a new lithium-manganese-rich battery pack before they assembled the first physical prototype. That helped the concept move to an approved program in one month.

Such speed will help GM save costs as it races to preserve profitability amid a historic upheaval in the automotive industry. But will it be enough to catapult it back into the leadership position it once enjoyed?

The rise of Chinese automakers won’t make it easy. Their factories are capable of producing far more than Chinese consumers can absorb, and coupled with government subsidies and cheaper labor, these vehicles have flooded markets from Europe to South America with inexpensive vehicles.

Chinese automaker’s cost advantage is so steep that, without trade barriers, “they will pretty much demolish most other companies in the world,” Elon Musk said in a 2024 earnings call. In response, he has been trying to pivot Tesla from an automotive company to an AI and robotics company.
GM’s move into autonomy signals a similar shift. But to deliver true autonomy, GM realized it didn’t have the platform it needed. With a new architecture, it should have a fighting chance.
